frozen_question: Why did JForex IHistory.getTicks return 0 ticks for USATECH.IDX/USD on 2025-10-01T14:00:00Z..15:00:00Z when the official Dukascopy Historical Data Export returned 22,985 BID ticks for the same interval?

key_observations.claim: Dukascopy historical data exist for the frozen interval.
key_observations.observation: Official Historical Data Export contained 22,985 BID tick rows from 14:00:00 through 14:59:59 UTC; 0 rows outside interval.

key_observations.claim: Initial JForex READ_A encountered provider/cache transport timeout.
key_observations.observation: CurvesJsonProtocolHandler Read timed out / SocketTimeoutException; no valid ticks or payload.

key_observations.claim: Exact local cache chunk exists and is zero bytes.
Zero-byte chunk creation temporally coincides with the initial timeout.
key_observations.observation: Initial READ_A ran 19:02:58.741Z..19:04:01.827Z; zero-byte chunk created at 19:04:00.170Z.

key_observations.claim: READ_A-R1 later returned zero ticks without changing the zero-byte chunk.
key_observations.observation: READ_A-R1 ran 20:23:45.445Z..20:24:03.817Z and ended BLOCKED_JF02_EMPTY_RESPONSE; cache chunk retained original 19:04:00.170Z modified time and size 0.

key_observations.claim: Official JForex 2.13.99 semantics say getTicks blocks until data are loaded from server into local cache, then read into collection.
key_observations.observation: IHistory.getTicks documented as synchronous server-to-local-cache load followed by read; JFException on loading error.

key_observations.claim: DEMO historical data are expected to come from LIVE history.
key_observations.observation: Dukascopy states DEMO real-time ticks differ from LIVE, but historical data on DEMO are returned from LIVE environment.
Collector used setSubscribedInstruments(..., true); official docs say true waits for subscription. Log showed SUBSCRIBED INSTRUMENTS: [USATECH.IDX/USD].

key_observations.claim: Runtime dependency versions are internally coherent.
key_observations.observation: DDS2-jClient-JForex 3.6.51 resolved JForex-API 2.13.99; runtime reported API implementation version 2.13.99.

key_observations.claim: getTicks call path uses JForex cache stack.
key_observations.observation: History.getTicks -> HistoryData.getTicksSecured -> IFeedDataProvider.loadTicksDataSynched -> LoadDataAction -> CurvesDataLoader.loadInCache -> LocalCacheManager.readData.

candidate_causes.basis: Instrument resolved/subscribed as USATECH.IDX/USD; exact cache path USATECHIDXUSD created; D1 used same provider instrument.
No instrument-specific official guarantee located; however SDK accepted/subscribed symbol and attempted exact history chunk load.
Official Dukascopy documentation states DEMO historical data come from LIVE environment.
A software defect cannot be excluded, but no direct version-specific failure evidence found.
Resolved API dependency and observed runtime implementation both 2.13.99.
Initial timeout created the exact requested chunk as zero bytes; subsequent call produced empty response.
Persistent zero-byte exact-hour cache file survived into READ_A-R1; static call path proves getTicks relies on disk cache stack.
Blocking subscription requested and observed as subscribed before history access.
Official from/to semantics are inclusive; collector used [start,end-exclusive) by setting to=end_ms-1, and D1 proves data throughout that hour.
No direct evidence of index-specific restriction; remains possible but secondary.
Initial read directly observed a network timeout in CurvesJsonProtocolHandler; likely upstream trigger of bad cache state.
Official demo JNLP/SDK connected successfully; dependency versions coherent; no mismatch evidence found.
Cannot exclude undocumented server/cache semantics around failed chunks.
Static inspection shows official getTicks path, correct instrument binding, blocking subscription, and correct frozen interval; failure reproduces inside provider cache layer.

most_supported_root_cause.detailed_hypothesis: The initial provider/cache download timed out and left the exact 14h tick chunk as a persistent zero-byte file. The later synchronous getTicks request traversed the JForex disk-cache path and returned an empty tick collection without refreshing that zero-byte chunk.
most_supported_root_cause.why_not_proven: D2 forbids cache mutation/configuration mutation and any new history request, so no controlled cache-neutral counterfactual was executed.

repair_necessity.reason: Current JForex evidence path can silently yield zero ticks for an interval proven non-empty; fail-closed qualification cannot proceed without a controlled cache-state test.

minimum_next_experiment.title: CACHE-NEUTRAL CONTROLLED CAUSAL TEST V0.1
